body:
Lost ability to check for failures on this line.
Missing boolean or HRESULT return.
Should not return void, since we have no way to propagate errors out of this function.

this code no longer calls finish_input_device. Why did this move from here to the middle of the read loop: there might be cases other than `AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED` in which the user wishes to finish the current input device and switch.

This is part of the new case, from what I can tell (the old code used `ERR_BREAK(hr != S_OK)`). I want to understand the implication of calling finish_input_device() only here and in the similar if / else in the surrounding code.

The fact that this if/else does not handle `hr == AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED`, while the outer GetNextPacketSize does handle this, is a bit confusing. I might suggest to switch to a do / while or consider a different control flow, such as exposing `hr` out of the while loop, so that all three cases (GetNextPacketSIze, GetBuffer and the per-loop GetNextPacketSize) can handle the finish_input_device case the same.

This line is added. Can you explain a bit more why it is necessary to reset avail_frames in this case, given that the audio device is closed? The application may still want to read whatever frames would have been available.
